rootCauseGroups.name: Zero-evidence sites sent to Claude tiebreaker
rootCauseGroups.description: score < 15 AND neg < 30 — no restaurant evidence, no disqualifying evidence, so Claude is called. Claude returns plausible_unverified because it can't disprove either way.

proposedFix.description: Raise isAmbiguous minimum: don't invoke Claude when restaurantSignalScore < 15. Return plausible_unverified_fallback immediately. Sites with zero positive evidence should not spend tokens on Claude and should not get a 'pass' they haven't earned.
proposedFix.change: Add condition: if restaurantSignalScore < 15, return false (not ambiguous — just unknown)
proposedFix.riskNote: A restaurant with a completely dead website (score=0) would stop getting Claude's tiebreaker. But those sites already get plausible_unverified_fallback anyway — no behavior change for legitimate restaurants.

rootCauseGroups.name: High neg + high score conflict — no DQ rule fires
rootCauseGroups.description: score >= 40 AND neg >= 40. Current clear_non_fit rules only fire when neg is HIGH and score is LOW. These sites have genuinely high restaurant vocabulary (hotels with restaurants, 'reserve your car' UX) AND high negative vocabulary — no rule covers the conflict.

examples.why: Car rental: 'reservations' fires +15 everywhere in booking UX
Hotel chain: genuine restaurants inside hotels
Plumbing: 'book now', hours, phone identical to restaurant
Paint: 'find your color' + store hours + phone

proposedFix.description: Add rule: if negativeSignalScore > restaurantSignalScore AND negativeSignalScore >= 70 → clear_non_fit. When negative evidence EXCEEDS restaurant evidence by a clear margin and negative score is high, the site should be rejected regardless of absolute restaurant score.
proposedFix.change: Insert before verified_restaurant rules: if (negativeSignalScore >= 70 && negativeSignalScore > restaurantSignalScore) → clear_non_fit
proposedFix.riskNote: A bakery/brewery that has 'wholesale' (+20 neg) plus is 'booking a table' might have neg=70, score=80 — neg < score so rule would not fire. But must test carefully.

rootCauseGroups.name: Hotels/luxury hospitality — restaurant vocabulary from in-hotel dining
rootCauseGroups.description: score 27-60, neg 20-50. Luxury hotel chains (IHG, Rocco Forte, Taj, Shangri-La, Aman, Edition, Accor, Design Hotels) score high because they genuinely describe multiple restaurants, bars, chefs, tasting menus. STRONG_NEGATIVE_TEXT catches 'hotel rooms', 'book your stay', 'guest rooms' — but restaurant vocabulary overwhelms.

proposedFix.description: Add hotel-brand signals to STRONG_NEGATIVE_TEXT (+20): 'hotel collection', 'resort collection', 'hotel group', 'hotel brand', 'number of rooms', 'property portfolio', 'loyalty program', 'points redemption'. Also add moderate negatives (+10): 'book a room', 'check-in date', 'check-out date', 'nightly rate', 'room type'.
proposedFix.riskNote: A standalone restaurant in a hotel (e.g., a restaurant that happens to mention 'loyalty program' in a partnership) is edge case. But 'nightly rate', 'check-in date', 'book a room' are unambiguous hotel signals.

rootCauseGroups.name: Travel/car rental — 'reserve' UX fires STRONG_POSITIVE_NAV
rootCauseGroups.description: score 18-48, neg 20-30. budget.com, avis.com, awaytravel.com, trivago.com, oyster.com (already counted in B and C). Core problem: 'reserve your car', 'book now', 'reservations' in car rental booking UX fires the same +15 nav signal as a restaurant reservation CTA.

proposedFix.description: Add to STRONG_NEGATIVE_TEXT (+20): 'car rental', 'rental car', 'rent a car', 'reserve your vehicle', 'rental agreement', 'luggage', 'baggage'. Add to MODERATE_NEGATIVE_TEXT (+10): 'pick-up location', 'drop-off', 'free cancellation' (travel context).

rootCauseGroups.name: Fitness/wellness studios — class booking UX fires same signals as restaurant
rootCauseGroups.description: score 0-25, neg 0-30. SoulCycle, CorePower Yoga, Pure Barre, Snap Fitness, 9Round. 'Reserve a spot', 'book a class', hours, phone — identical reservation pattern to restaurants. The fitness industry gap in negative signals.

proposedFix.description: Add to STRONG_NEGATIVE_TEXT (+20): 'fitness class', 'yoga class', 'workout class', 'personal training', 'gym membership', 'class schedule'. Add to MODERATE_NEGATIVE_TEXT (+10): 'instructor', 'studio membership', 'class pass', 'unlimited classes'.
proposedFix.riskNote: Restaurants rarely mention 'fitness class' or 'gym membership'. 'Instructor' might appear on cooking class pages — guard with context.

rootCauseGroups.name: Fashion/retail/home furnishings — furniture 'dining' and retail 'book appointment'
rootCauseGroups.description: score 6-51, neg 20-60. Pottery Barn, Crate&Barrel, West Elm score high because 'dining table', 'bar cart', 'wine rack', 'brunch collection' fire restaurant keywords. Fashion sites (Rent the Runway, Everlane, Patagonia, Bombas, Urban Outfitters) have lower scores but leak through Claude.

proposedFix.description: Add to STRONG_NEGATIVE_TEXT (+20): 'add to bag', 'add to cart', 'free returns', 'return policy', 'size guide'. Add to MODERATE_NEGATIVE_TEXT (+10): 'free shipping', 'new arrivals', 'shop the collection', 'limited edition'.
proposedFix.riskNote: Restaurant merch stores could have 'add to cart' — but those are clearly restaurant sites already scored high on other signals.

rootCauseGroups.name: Remaining miscellaneous
rootCauseGroups.description: Home services (Merry Maids, Molly Maid, ServiceMaster), real estate (HotPads, Boston Properties), finance (Vanguard), travel (Oyster reviews), home products (Kohler, Sherwin-Williams partially covered in B). Many already have moderate negative signals but score leaks through Claude at low scores.

proposedFix.description: Combination: Fix A (isAmbiguous threshold) catches the zero-score ones. Fix B (neg > score rule) catches high-neg ones. Add 'maid service', 'cleaning service', 'damage restoration' to STRONG_NEGATIVE_TEXT for home services. Add specific domains (oyster.com is a hotel review site — add to KNOWN_NON_RESTAURANT_DOMAINS).
